test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A conical vessel has base radius 6 cm and height 20 cm. Water is poured into the vessel until it is 3/4 full. Find the volume (in cm³) of water in the vessel.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of full **conical vessel** = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Volume = (1/3) × π × 6² × 20 = (1/3) × π × 36 × 20 = 12 × 20 × π = 240π cm³

Volume of water = (3/4) × Total Volume = (3/4) × 240π

Volume of water = 3 × 60π = 180π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 180π cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Base radius** (r) = 6 cm

**Height** (h) = 20 cm

**Water level** = 3/4 full

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b5bd456ad2756908c805671f437173dc299ebe0d00062d2203e56aecfdcfbff.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cone (V) = (1/3)πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of vessel = (1/3) × π × (6)² × 20

⇒ Total capacity = (1/3) × π × 36 × 20

⇒ Total capacity = 12 × 20 × π = 240π cm³

⇒ Volume of water poured = 3/4 × Total capacity

⇒ Volume of water = (3/4) × 240π

⇒ Volume of water = 3 × 60π = 180π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 180π cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of Cone

The slant height (l) is given by l = √(r² + h²), representing the distance from the apex to the edge of the base.

Surface Area of Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl and Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(l + r).

Relationship with Cylinder

The volume of a cone is exactly 1/3 the volume of a **cylinder** with the same base radius and height.</p
